 Predicted line-ups for Premier League teams in Matchweek 10
 Ben Bloom
 06 Nov 2026
 See which players we think will start for their clubs this weekend
 Football writer Ben Bloom is predicting how every Premier League team will line up in Matchweek 10. 
 Click on the following links to jump to the relevant match
 NFOMCI | BHABRE | CRYLIV | IPSBOU | SUNCHE | MUNAVL 
 See:  Injury updates for every club and player 
 See: Who's suspended or close to a ban? 
 Nott'm Forest v Man City predicted line-ups 
 Nott'm Forest:  Goals continue to be Forest’s primary issue, so it will be interesting to see if Oliver Glasner switches things up in the attacking end. Igor Jesus has trained all week and “looked good”, according to the manager, but Nicolas Dominguez has been ruled out for eight weeks. Daniel Munoz will hope to return to the starting XI, while Ousmane Diomande could also earn a recall.
 Man City: Marc Guehi started in midweek, but lost his Premier League spot last weekend and could miss out again here in a battle for one centre-back spot with Abdukodir Khusanov. Ayyoub Bouaddi came off the bench on Wednesday night, and he could well start there again, with Enzo Fernandez moved back to accommodate another attacking player. As always, there is not enough room for all of Enzo Maresca’s attacking players.

 Brighton v Brentford predicted line-ups 
 Brighton: Having seen off Man City last weekend, expect a similar looking line-up here, if not exactly the same. Fabian Hurzeler said he has a “big hope” that Ferdi Kadioglu is available, but Costinha or Mats Wieffer will start at right-back if not. Hurzeler has more attacking options available now with the return of Jack Hinshelwood and Yankuba Minteh, while Maxim De Cuyper can move back into defence, but few changes appear likely.
 Brentford: There is no guarantee of Yehor Yarmoliuk’s recall on his return from suspension, but he will hope to displace Mamadou Sangare. Jaidon Anthony could earn a starting spot at the expense of Dango Ouattara, but it was a strong Brentford victory last weekend so Keith Andrews may well keep much of his team the same.
 Back to top 
 Crystal Palace v Liverpool predicted line-ups 
 Crystal Palace: Jean-Philippe Mateta’s suspension means one of Jorgen Strand Larsen or Eddie Nketiah will lead the line. Axel Disasi was omitted from midweek duties after an unspecified 'internal decision', but Pierre Sage confirmed he will be available for this. Quentin Timber returned from injury in that match, which saw Daichi Kamada move higher up the pitch and Dwight McNeil miss out. Oscar Mingueza versus Anan Khalaili seems like a 50/50 call.
 Liverpool: Andoni Iraola must decide what to do with Dominik Szoboszlai. The Hungarian played as a No 10 in midweek, but with Florian Wirtz expected to return to the starting line-up he must either replace Trey Nyoni or Alexis Mac Allister in central midfield, shift position again, or return to the bench. Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz look set for substitute roles.
 Back to top 
 Ipswich v AFC Bournemouth predicted line-ups 
 Ipswich: Sasa Lukic did not make it back in time for last weekend, but could well return. If that is from the outset then one of Florentino Luis or Exequiel Palacios will make way. The remainder of the team looks fairly settled aside from the left winger position, where Jaden Philogene is just about keeping out Daizen Maeda and Jack Clarke. At some point, Emersonn could make way for Zian Flemming up front.
 Bournemouth: Marco Rose continued his usual midweek rotation, while securing another victory, but all his big guns will return on Sunday. The only two question marks are whether Junior Kroupi is ready to start after gaining minutes off the bench, and who, of Ryan Christie and Lewis Cook, gets the nod in central midfield. Alex Scott could return to the matchday squad for the first time.
 Back to top 
 Sunderland v Chelsea predicted line-ups 
 Sunderland: Sunderland will be without the suspended Omar Alderete and injured Habib Diarra, but Regis Le Bris suggested Nordi Mukiele “should be available” after missing the last two games. Assuming Mukiele starts at centre-back, Luke O’Nien and Kevin Danso are fighting for one spot. There is uncertainty over the occupants of both winger positions, where Le Bris has a range of options, none of which have delivered much of late. 
 Chelsea: Estevao impressed when handed an unexpected start last weekend and will hope to retain his place in a largely unchanged line-up. Moises Caicedo is not certain to play due to calf discomfort, while Xabi Alonso must decide whether to bring back Jordan Henderson, who missed out last time through illness. Pep Chavarria and Marco Palestra will battle for the left-back spot. Emiliano Martinez has returned to training and a late decision will be made on his availability. 
 Back to top 
 Man Utd v Aston Villa predicted line-ups 
 Man Utd:  Ayden Heaven or Matthijs De Ligt will start in place of the suspended Lisandro Martinez, while Michael Carrick made no mention of Harry Maguire in his pre-match press conference after the England centre-back appeared to be limping in midweek. Youri Tielemans or Andrey Santos will replace the injured Carlos Baleba, so long as Kobbie Mainoo can start again. There has been speculation that Shea Lacey may earn a first Premier League start in place of Amad.
 Aston Villa: Matty Cash is suspended and Aaron Wan-Bissaka faces a late fitness test, which could mean a rare start at right-back for Lamare Bogarde or the redeployment of another midfielder. Joao Gomes will battle Leon Goretzka and Ross Barkley for a spot in the middle of the pitch. Assuming John McGinn and Johan Manzambi retain their places, it leaves Alysson, Emiliano Buendia and Ibrahim Mbaye all in contention for the final attacking position.
